_note: Editorial record for the five case studies. Use the same eight-part structure on every case: Problem, Situation, Challenge, Approach, Work, Result, Service, Limitations. Items marked in 'verifyBeforePublishing' need owner evidence before the page is changed again.

caseStudies.title: Zero Idea: Facebook Page Recovery
caseStudies.problem: A Facebook Page with a large educational audience was taken over, and the legitimate administrator lost access.
caseStudies.situation: Zero Idea is a Facebook Page that publishes science and educational content, with over 400,000 followers.
caseStudies.challenge: The page was hacked and the administrator was locked out for about two months.
caseStudies.approach: I investigated how the compromise happened and confirmed the legitimate administrator's ownership of the page. Then I worked through the recovery route with the platform.
work: Confirmed the legitimate administrator's ownership of the page
Worked through the recovery process to restore administrator access
Secured the page against further compromise once access was restored
caseStudies.result: The page was recovered and the legitimate administrator regained control. The page owner later shared a public video acknowledging the recovery.
caseStudies.keyTakeaway: Long lockouts can sometimes be resolved with a structured, patient process, even when an attacker has taken control. Results still vary from case to case.
limitations: This case reflects one page and one set of circumstances. It does not predict the outcome of another case
Recovery depended on the evidence of ownership available and on platform decisions

caseStudies.title: Dinajpur Image: Page Restoration
caseStudies.problem: A content page was disabled after trademark and copyright reports that the page owner considered false.
caseStudies.situation: Dinajpur Image is a page focused on history and cultural content.
caseStudies.challenge: The page was disabled after the reports. The reporting party allegedly demanded money in connection with them.
caseStudies.approach: I reviewed the ownership and legitimacy of the page, then prepared the verification and dispute process.
caseStudies.keyTakeaway: When reports appear to be false, ownership verification and Meta's dispute process are the proper route. Results still depend on Meta's review.
limitations: Dispute outcomes depend on Meta's review and on the evidence provided
This case does not show how other copyright or trademark disputes will be decided
verifyBeforePublishing: Allegation about the reporting party (legal review)

caseStudies.title: Santali Ari-Chari: Community Page Recovery
caseStudies.clientType: Community page for Santali language and culture
caseStudies.problem: A community page was hacked, and its online presence was affected.
caseStudies.situation: Santali Ari-Chari is a page dedicated to Santali language and culture.
caseStudies.challenge: The page was compromised, and the community's online presence was at risk while access was in question.
caseStudies.approach: I assessed the compromise and confirmed the administrator's legitimate ownership of the page.
work: Completed account recovery and administrative restoration
Applied security improvements to reduce the risk of a repeat compromise
caseStudies.result: The page was recovered and the community's online presence was restored.
caseStudies.keyTakeaway: For a community page, securing access after recovery matters as much as getting it back.
limitations: Recovery steps depended on the evidence of ownership available at the time
Security improvements reduce risk. They do not remove it

caseStudies.title: Business Manager Verification: Anonymized Case
caseStudies.anonymizationNote: Client name and identifying details are withheld to protect confidentiality.
caseStudies.problem: A digital marketing business faced repeated Business Manager restrictions and could not complete verification.
caseStudies.situation: The business engaged me for Business Manager support.
caseStudies.challenge: The Business Manager had several restrictions and verification issues.
caseStudies.approach: I reviewed the restriction history and the current state of the Business Manager to find the path to verification.
work: Prepared the Business Manager for Meta's verification process
caseStudies.keyTakeaway: Verification is often blocked by unresolved restrictions rather than by the verification step itself. Resolving those first is usually the key step.
limitations: Client details are withheld, so the case is described in general terms
Verification decisions are made by Meta. This case does not predict another outcome

caseStudies.title: Delicious Food by Arpa: Multiple Platform Issues
caseStudies.platform: Meta Business Manager and Facebook Page
caseStudies.problem: A food business faced fake copyright claims, a restricted advertising account, and Business Manager verification issues at the same time.
caseStudies.situation: Delicious Food by Arpa is a food and cake business based in Bangladesh.
caseStudies.challenge: Several platform issues were blocking each other, so none could be resolved on its own.
caseStudies.approach: I reviewed each issue separately: the copyright claims, the advertising restriction, and the verification blockers. Then I chose the resolution route for each.
caseStudies.result: The copyright claims were removed, the advertising restriction was resolved, Business Manager verification was completed, and Facebook Page verification was assisted.
caseStudies.keyTakeaway: Several connected platform issues can sometimes be handled together in one structured engagement, rather than as separate efforts.
limitations: Each issue depended on platform decisions and on the evidence available
This case does not predict the outcome for another account
verifyBeforePublishing: Client permission to name the business
